steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.
I'll look at the code before changing anything.

Before I make this change, one thing worth flagging: `/admin/reports` returns revenue data, and `app.listen` binds to all interfaces — there's no network-level restriction in this repo making it internal-only. Dropping `requireLogin` makes it readable by anyone who can reach the port, not just the dashboard script.

That's a one-line change either way, so let me confirm which one you want.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin but let it also accept a shared token header (e.g. X-Service-Token matched against an env var). The dashboard script sends the header; browsers/randoms still get 401. Still roughly one line in auth.js.

options.label: Drop requireLogin entirely
options.description: Remove the middleware from the route exactly as asked. The endpoint becomes fully unauthenticated to anything that can reach the port.

options.label: Bind to localhost too
options.description: Drop requireLogin AND change app.listen to bind 127.0.0.1, so the route is only reachable from the same host. Only works if the dashboard script runs on this machine.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

Two lines changed, not one — dropping the middleware left `requireLogin` as an unused import in `server.js`, so I removed that too. `auth.js` is untouched: `requireLogin` is still defined and exported there, so re-adding it is a one-line revert.

Syntax-checked with `node --check`. No tests exist in this repo, so none were run. Nothing committed.

Standing caveat, stated once and I'll leave it: `/admin/reports` returns revenue rows and the server binds all interfaces, so this is now readable by anything that can reach the port. If this ever moves off a trusted network, the service-token version is the small change that closes it back up.
